newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks rise in mid-week trading.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks rise in mid-week trading.

text.p: Cyprus shares rose sharply on mid-week trading on Wednesday, with significant gains in banking stocks.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) general index, set at 100 points, closed at 85.17, gaining 0.95 points, or 1.13 percent in one trading session.
On Friday the market closed at 83.78.
The banking sub index gained 3.16 percent, closing at 95.06 from 92.14 on Friday.
The Bank of Cyprus closed at 356.5, adding 11 cents on its fully paid shares from Friday's close of 345.5.
Earlier on Wednesday the bank said its convertible 40 million pound bond issue listed on the Luxembourg stock exchange had been over subscribed by foreign investors 3.6 times.

The bank will offer convertible bonds worth 10 million pounds to shareholders in November in a drive to raise capital for further expansion into Greece, bank chairman Solon Triantafyllides told a news conference.
Fully-paid shares in the Cyprus Popular Bank stood at 341, gaining 10.5 cents over last week's closing figure of 330.5. Fully paid shares of Hellenic Bank closed at 276.5 from 269 on Friday.

No transactions were made in shares of Keo Ltd, the Cypriot beer and wine producer which on Tuesday announced pre-tax losses of 393,000 pounds in the first half of the year. The company said that prospects for the second half appeared better.
The index of the insurance sector closed at 61.93 from 61.27 on Friday. Universal Life Insurance closed at 386.5 from 380. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid remained unchanged at 138.5.
Fully paid shares in subsidiary Interamerican Insurance closed half a cent lower at 103.5.
